newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan energy firm to sell garbage fuel technology.
newsitem.headline: Japan energy firm to sell garbage fuel technology.

text.p: Japan's Electric Power Development Co said on Tuesday it plans to market to local governments technology for generating electric power from garbage.

A spokesman for the company, which is two-thirds owned by the government, said it will build a 3.5 billion yen ($30.7 million) pilot plant in the western Japan city of Kitakyushu in late August to generate electricity using refuse-derived fuel (RDF), which is made from household garbage.
It will begin marketing the facility's technology to local governments in the business year starting in April 1999.
The spokesman said the new system can also significantly reduce emissions of dioxin, a highly toxic by-product of some industrial processes and waste combustion.
It hopes to make the new power generation system its mainstay business as it heads towards scheduled privatisation five years from now, he said.
The Japanese government currently holds a majority stake in Electric Power Development Co. The remainder is held by Japanese electric power utilities, including Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc.
